system.text:
You are a senior software engineer on a team that maintains a production Python codebase. You
have been handed one change request. You own it from understanding the requirement to delivering
code that a reviewer can approve and merge.

Your responsibilities

Understand the requirement.
- Read the request as the product team means it, not only its literal words. Work out the inputs,
  the expected outputs, the error cases and the edge cases it implies.
- Where the request is ambiguous, choose the interpretation most consistent with the rest of the
  system and with what users of the feature would expect.

Understand the code before changing it.
- Read the code you are changing and the code it depends on or that depends on it, as far as it is
  available to you. Know what a function does from its code, not only from its name.
- Know who calls what you change. Keep public interfaces, data formats and behaviour that other code
  relies on intact unless the request asks you to change them.

Make the change correctly.
- Correctness comes first: the new behaviour must be right for every input the request implies,
  including empty, missing, zero, negative, very large and malformed values where relevant.
- Handle errors the way the codebase does: fail clearly on invalid input; never silently return
  wrong data.
- Treat money, dates, units and identifiers with care: exact arithmetic where the codebase uses it,
  explicit units, no lossy conversions.
- Don't introduce security problems: validate untrusted input and keep secrets and personal data
  out of logs and output.

Keep the codebase healthy.
- Fit in with the surrounding code: its naming, structure, typing and error handling. A reviewer
  should not be able to tell which lines are new by their style.
- Keep the change as small as the request allows, and complete: every file the change needs, none
  it doesn't. Don't refactor, rename or reformat unrelated code.
- Write code that is simple and readable; add a docstring or comment where intent is not obvious.

Check your work.
- You cannot run the code, so verify it by reading it: trace the main path and each edge case
  through your change, check every import and name you use exists, and check that everything that
  calls the code you changed still works.
- Your change will be applied to the repository and checked by tests you do not see.

What you are given
- <task>: the change request from the product team.
- <context>: material from the repository. How much varies: it may be a single file or much of the
  project. It is what you know about the codebase.

What you can and cannot do
- You cannot run code, and there is no one to ask.
- If tools are provided with this request, you may use them to look at the repository before you
  answer. If no tools are provided, you cannot open files or search: deliver the finished change in
  this reply. Tool calls, plans and requests for more files written as text are not executed, and a
  reply without code counts as no change.
- If something you need is not shown, make the most reasonable assumption consistent with what is
  shown, and implement it.

Output format (strict)
Your reply is the code change itself. Return the complete new contents of every file you create or
modify, each wrapped exactly as:
<file path="PATH">
...full file contents...
</file>
- Replace PATH with the file's real path relative to the repository root, as shown in <context> or
  <task>.
- Always the whole file, never a diff or an excerpt, and no placeholders such as "rest unchanged".
- Files you don't change are left out.
- Return nothing outside the <file> blocks: no explanations, plans or summaries before or after them.

user.label: Task (change request)
user.text:
Checkout should only offer express delivery when the warehouse will really send the order by
express. Add `express_available(skus, sites, hazmat_skus)` in a new module
`shopkit/shipping/options.py`: `skus` are the cart's SKUs, `sites` the warehouse sites that could
ship it (warehouse.sites.Site), `hazmat_skus` the SKUs classed as dangerous goods. Return True when
the warehouse would put an order with these SKUs into an express wave, False otherwise.

"""Pick waves: paid orders are grouped into waves per site and allocated to bins before pickers
get their lists. Released waves go to the WMS (core.order_engine.handleWmsCallback brings status back)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import time
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta

from shopkit.config import SETTINGS, Settings
from shopkit.events import BUS, EventBus
from shopkit.orders.models import Order
from shopkit.warehouse.sites import Lot, Site, SiteStock

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

EXPRESS, STANDARD = "express", "standard"
MAX_WAVE_ORDERS = 200
MAX_WAVE_LINES = 1200
SHORT_PICK_TOLERANCE = 0          # units an order may be short and still ship (ops set it to 0 after INC-2418)
OVERSELL_ALERT_UNITS = 5


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WaveOrder:
    order: Order
    service: str = STANDARD                 # express | standard
    paid_at: datetime | None = None
    country: str = "US"
    gift: bool = False
    hold: str = ""                          # fraud review, address check... non-empty = not allocatable


@dataclass
class Allocation:
    order_id: str
    sku: str
    site: str
    bin: str

    it is split across sites line by line; else what's missing is backordered and the rest waits

    first and a site's safety stock is never allocated.

def test_feed_updates_hold_big_price_jumps_and_never_touch_titles():
    products = {"MUG-1": Product("MUG-1", "Blue mug", 2000), "TEA-9": Product("TEA-9", "Tea", 1000)}
    items = parse_feed('{"items": [{"sku": "mug-1", "price_cents": 2100, "available": false},'
                       ' {"sku": "TEA9", "price_cents": 199}, {"sku": "X1", "price_cents": 5}, {"sku": "Y"}]}')
    held = []
    report = apply_updates(items, products, on_hold=lambda *a: held.append(a))
    assert report.updated == ["MUG-1"] and products["MUG-1"].price_cents == 2100 and not products["MUG-1"].active
    assert report.held == [("TEA-9", 1000, 199)] and held == [("TEA-9", 1000, 199)]
    assert products["TEA-9"].price_cents == 1000 and report.unknown == ["X-1"] and len(report.errors) == 1
    dry = apply_updates([{"sku": "tea 9", "price_cents": 900}], products, dry_run=True)
    assert dry.updated == ["TEA-9"] and products["TEA-9"].price_cents == 1000
    diff = diff_sheet("sku,title,price\nMUG1,Blue mug XL,21.00\nNEW1,New,1.00\n", products)
    assert diff == {"new": ["NEW-1"], "price": [], "title": ["MUG-1"]}

from datetime import date, datetime

from shopkit.config import Settings
from shopkit.core.order_engine import OrderRecord, splitForShipping
from shopkit.events import EventBus
from shopkit.orders.models import Order, OrderLine
from shopkit.warehouse.sites import Lot, Site, SiteStock
from shopkit.warehouse.waves import EXPRESS, STANDARD, WaveOrder, allocate_wave, pick_list_text, release

TODAY = date(2026, 3, 10)
MAIN = Site("MAIN", "Main", priority=0)
EAST = Site("EAST", "East", priority=1, services=frozenset({"air"}))


def _stock(*lots):
    return SiteStock([Lot(*l) for l in lots])


def _o(oid, *lines, **kw):
    return WaveOrder(Order(oid, [OrderLine(s, q, 100) for s, q in lines]), **kw)


def test_single_site_fefo_and_waves_per_service():
    stock = _stock(("MUG", "MAIN", "A1", 5, date(2026, 6, 1)), ("MUG", "MAIN", "A2", 5, date(2026, 4, 1)),
                   ("MUG", "EAST", "B1", 5))
    bus = EventBus()
    res = allocate_wave([_o("O1", ("MUG", 6), service=EXPRESS, paid_at=datetime(2026, 3, 9)),
                         _o("O2", ("MUG", 1), paid_at=datetime(2026, 3, 8))], [MAIN, EAST], stock, today=TODAY, bus=bus)
    express = next(w for w in res.waves if w.service == EXPRESS)
    assert [(a.bin, a.qty) for a in express.allocations] == [("A2", 5), ("A1", 1)]
    assert {w.service for w in res.waves} == {EXPRESS, STANDARD} and res.stats["single_site"] == 2


def test_hazmat_only_from_ground_sites_and_never_express():
    stock = _stock(("BATT", "EAST", "B1", 5), ("BATT", "MAIN", "A1", 1))
    bus = EventBus()
    res = allocate_wave([_o("O1", ("BATT", 1), service=EXPRESS)], [MAIN, EAST], stock, today=TODAY,
                        hazmat_skus=frozenset({"BATT"}), bus=bus)
    assert [(w.site, w.service) for w in res.waves] == [("MAIN", STANDARD)]
    assert any(e.name == "order.service_downgraded" for e in bus.history)
    res2 = allocate_wave([_o("O2", ("BATT", 3))], [MAIN, EAST], stock, today=TODAY, hazmat_skus=frozenset({"BATT"}),
                         bus=EventBus())
    assert res2.backordered == {"O2": {"BATT": 3}}            # EAST has 5 but only ships by air


def test_split_backorder_gift_and_safety_stock():
    stock = _stock(("MUG", "MAIN", "A1", 2), ("MUG", "EAST", "B1", 2), ("TEA", "MAIN", "A9", 1))
    res = allocate_wave([_o("O1", ("MUG", 3)), _o("O2", ("TEA", 2))], [MAIN, EAST], stock, today=TODAY, bus=EventBus())
    assert res.stats["split"] == 1 and res.backordered == {"O2": {"TEA": 1}}
    gift = allocate_wave([_o("G1", ("MUG", 1), gift=True)], [MAIN, EAST], _stock(("MUG", "MAIN", "A1", 1)),
                         today=TODAY, bus=EventBus())
    assert gift.stats["single_site"] == 1
    g2 = allocate_wave([_o("G2", ("MUG", 3), gift=True)], [MAIN, EAST], _stock(("MUG", "MAIN", "A1", 2), ("MUG", "EAST", "B", 2)),
                       today=TODAY, bus=EventBus())
    assert "G2" in g2.backordered and g2.waves == []
    safe = Site("MAIN", "Main", safety_stock=2)
    res3 = allocate_wave([_o("O3", ("MUG", 2))], [safe], _stock(("MUG", "MAIN", "A1", 3)), today=TODAY, bus=EventBus())
    assert res3.backordered == {"O3": {"MUG": 1}}


def test_expired_lots_holds_and_shadow_split():
    stock = _stock(("MILK", "MAIN", "C1", 4, date(2026, 3, 1)), ("MILK", "MAIN", "C2", 1, date(2026, 3, 20)))
    calls = []
    def shadow(order, avail):
        calls.append(order.id)
        return splitForShipping(OrderRecord(order.id, lines=[{"sku": l.sku, "qty": l.qty} for l in order.lines]), avail)
    res = allocate_wave([_o("O1", ("MILK", 2)), _o("O2", ("MILK", 1), hold="fraud review")], [MAIN], stock,
                        today=TODAY, bus=EventBus(), shadow_split=shadow)
    assert res.backordered == {"O1": {"MILK": 1}} and res.skipped == {"O2": "hold: fraud review"}


def test_release_and_pick_list():
    stock = _stock(("MUG", "MAIN", "A1", 5))
    res = allocate_wave([_o("O1", ("MUG", 2))], [MAIN], stock, today=TODAY, bus=EventBus(), metrics={})
    w = res.waves[0]
    payload = release(w, bus=EventBus())
    assert payload["picks"] == [{"order": "O1", "sku": "MUG", "bin": "A1", "qty": 2}]
    assert "A1" in pick_list_text(w) and "1 orders, 2 units" in pick_list_text(w)
